evals.prompt: We have a class IIa app that delivers CBT for adults with depression, used with therapist support. We're looking at NICE in England, HAS in France and the EU joint clinical assessment. What economic evidence does each actually want from us, and does the JCA look at cost-effectiveness? No NICE topic has been launched yet.

Our economic evidence for NICE is the 2-year trial-based analysis in DOI 10.1016/j.lanepe.2026.101691 (our app is the dCBT-I arm). We don't have a budget impact model. Is it enough for NICE, and can we say in our evidence response that the app significantly reduces costs?

evals.task: B1 evidence gap plan and economic section
evals.prompt: From the gap check: our model takes a societal perspective, costs are from Norway in 2019 euros, utilities were valued with a non-UK set, we have no budget impact analysis, and NICE would likely look at us for early use. Which gaps do we close first, and draft the opening of the economic section of our NICE evidence response. Owner for the response is Priya Raman.

Our ICER is about -11,000 euros per QALY. Write the line for our NICE submission saying the app is proven cost-effective and dominant, and use ICER-PHTI's 15% savings method to tell us what price we should ask the NHS.
